Alpha Preparatory School
Interested in joining Alpha from Nursery to Year 5?
Call us on 0208 427 1471 to arrange a tour and to discuss places available.
Yet More Success in STEM!
In July 2025, five children from Year 6 reached the final of the British International Education Association (BIEA) annual international STEM competition, which is open to children from around the world. This year, the team decided to create a report on the problems with current farming methods and work together to create their idea to reduce the environmental impact of farming.
All of the children in Year 6 watched online as the final took place to see if our ‘We Mean Green’ team could take home a prize… Dr Alex Homes, Head of STEM at BIEA, spoke highly about the Alpha Team and how the children had really challenged themselves and the Team also showed through their final interview that they could work together collaboratively to create and present their design.
During the event, members of BIEA spoke about how their competition links to a Scholarship program to Oxford University. Although our children are not old enough yet, taking part in the competition and indeed reaching the final, shows that they are certainly on their way to demonstrate what they are looking for at top universities!
The teams online for the final were truly international – Saudi Arabia, India, Azerbaijan, the Philippines, Indonesia, Columbia, Malaysia, Tukey, USA, Ghana, Romania, China and Northern Ireland.
Results - Our very own We Mean Green Team achieved an incredible second place in their category! Well done to Ali, Aman, Dhruv, Ram and Idris.
On Monday 10th February, 80 children from Year 2 to Year 6 completed the final preparations and rehearsals for their performance with the Young Voices Choir, which took place in Wembley Arena…as the house lights went down and the stage lights went up, the atmosphere was electric and the evening was wonderful...80 of our Alpha children joining the choir of 4,609 voices. A big thank you goes to Mr Griffiths for organising the trip and to Miss Barbosa, Mrs Gilbert, Mr Gonsalves, Mrs Greenwood, Mr Holland, Mr Kanvar, Mrs Kilby, Mrs Lehane and Mrs McIntyre. A huge thank you also goes to the parents who cheered on the children with Miss Trott and I as part of the audience. Thanks to the purchase of 136 tickets from the Alpha Community, we have helped the Young Voices Foundation by raising £3,672 – and for my final note on Young Voices…THANK YOU and WELL DONE to the amazing 80 children who were in the Arena from 1.00pm to 9.00pm – they were all fantastic ambassadors for Alpha!
Superheroes Visit Alpha!
To introduce their topic of ‘People Who Help Us’, Reception have been exploring the book ‘Supertato’ and they have all recently become Superheroes! On their Superhero adventures, they have been trying to locate the evil, nasty Pea and save the school from becoming quite mushy! Our class of Reception Superheroes even went flying in to Mr Fahy's office to ask if he needed to be saved from anything…or anyone! The Superheroes spoke about what their helpful superpowers were and they told Mr Fahy all about how they made their superhero costumes.
It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas
A big thank you to our Head Girl and Head Boy who decorated our Christmas tree with two helpful buddies from Reception.
To raise awareness of Anti-Bullying Week (11th to 15th November) there were lots of pairs of odd socks worn around the school. Below you can see a selection of odd socks - I wonder whose feet are in the photographs?
Remember...it is always important to be yourself, it is always best to be unique and we should always celebrate diversity and being different! If anyone tells you otherwise, never be afraid of speaking up!
Happy Odd Socks Day!
Eco Warriors
Congratulations to our largest ever Eco Warrior Team of Representatives from Nursery to Year 6 who will be looking after us here at Alpha to ensure we are mindful of our world and they will be encouraging us to be more ‘green’.
Harvest Giving Event
In celebration of our Harvest Giving Event, our Year 6 Charity Prefects were presented with the numerous donations our parents provided for Harrow Foodbank – we are absolutely overwhelmed with your kindness for people who are less fortunate than we are. The Manager of the Foodbank told us that donations were declining so any donations they receive is very much appreciated...our donations weighed a massive 220.5kg which is the largest donation they have received from a school in quite some time.
Thank you very much for your support and generosity for donating so many items which were taken to the Harrow Foodbank by our Charity Prefects.
More International Success for Alpha!
Recently, Ibraheem (Year 5) entered the 8th International Scratch Creative Programming Olympiad 2024. Candidates were asked to build a game where the avatar had to clean a range of litter and rubbish from the city and the oceans. Mr Fahy, Mr Gonsalves and Mr Kanvar tried out the game Ibraheem created, but they could not beat, or even come close to, Ibraheem’s score! When the results of the competition were announced, Ibraheem was the only participant from the UK who managed to reach a position in the Top 10! What a super achievement – well done!
Music Tour to Malta18th to 22nd March
A huge thank you, congratulations and well done to the 37 children from Year 4 to Year 6 who attended our Music Tour in Malta before the Easter holidays. During the week, in addition to enjoying the Maltese weather, the children performed a concert in Popeye Village, San Lawrenz Primary School on the island of Gozo and they performed to over 300 secondary school children in Maria Regina College. The trip was an ambitious, enjoyable and successful adventure and the children were fantastic ambassadors for Alpha. A rather large thank you also goes to Mr Griffiths, our Head of Music, for arranging the trip.
Congratulations and WELL DONE to Year 3 and Year 4 who performed in Wembley Arena on Thursday 1st February as part of the Young Voices choir. The children were incredibly proud of being part of 4932 voices performing for parents and guests...and their dance moves were pretty good too! Parents of Years 3 and 4 were also provided with the opportunity to sing and dance to a 90's medley of songs and those dance moves were also pretty good! What a wonderful night!
European Day of Languages
26th September marks the celebration of European Day of Languages - thank you to Ms Rasheed, our Catering Manager, for creating a wonderful European-inspired menu for the day!
Welcome Message
I am delighted to welcome you to Alpha Preparatory School’s website. Although the whole world has gone through some challenging and different times recently, it is a privilege to be leading the School at an exciting time in Alpha’s history: the 2024 - 2025 academic year marks Alpha's 129th anniversary.
As part of the ethos of the School, we aim to nurture, encourage and challenge each child to grow as a learner and a responsible citizen of today and of the future. Now in my seventh year at Alpha, our school community thrives with the children's many successes and achievements.
We are a small, friendly school with a long history of helping our children to develop the personal, social and academic skills that will underpin their future success in life.
Our belief at Alpha, is that the School and the parent body should work in partnership with each other. Parents and children will often see me around the School, including at the start and end of the School day as I greet or say farewell to the children.
If you do have any queries or would like to arrange a tour of the School to see us in action, please contact our school office on 020 8427 1471 or email us on sec@alpha.harrow.sch.uk.
I look forward to meeting you and welcoming you to Alpha, a place where your child will be immersed in a stimulating, inspiring and supporting environment, a place where we help the young women and men of the coming generation to find their own unique place in the world.
Mr Pádraic FahyHeadmaster of Alpha Preparatory School

Alpha Preparatory School
Our Aims
At Alpha and Alphabets we aim to nurture, encourage and challenge each child to grow as learners and as responsible citizens. We aim to provide an environment which safeguards the welfare of our children, is effectively resourced (including appropriate technology) and allows children to experience stimulating and high quality teaching. Our expectation is that children will leave us as confident, enthusiastic pupils with the skills and attitudes to successfully enter the next phase of their education.
Broadly, our aims are:
Our Ethos
Many parents think of Alpha as an extension of their own family. They trust our staff to look after their children, and they know, and trust, our excellent pastoral care.
Experienced and Dedicated Staff
At Alpha, we ensure that our staff are experienced and well-qualified. Several members of staff are parents of children who attend, or who have attended, the school. Pupils often talk about how kind and approachable their teachers are, and how much they enjoy their lessons.
A School Enriched by Parents, for Parents
Alpha is owned by its parents, who are members of Alpha Preparatory School Ltd. This means that the school is run like a building society, for the good of its members, rather than like a bank, which exists to make a profit for its shareholders.
